rationales.1: Sowing-window shelves group the rack before you read a single card, and every card parks price and stock on the same bottom line, which makes a season sweep fast and predictable.
rationales.2: Price, stock language and the bordered buy panel with quantity and Add to basket follow convention exactly on both surfaces.
rationales.3: The shipping limit is a bordered notice above the rack, out of stock is visibly marked, the germination estimate is labelled, and the unpriced packet reads Price on request.
rationales.4: Card text is legible and targets are generous, though the meta lines under each description run smaller than the surrounding body text.
rationales.5: One card and shelf system holds both surfaces, but the first shelf row does not share a baseline because the sweet-pea packet block runs taller, and the product page leaves a large empty field under the packet card.
rationales.6: The buy panel, year table, potting-shed notes and two companion cards give a first-time gardener everything needed without leaving the page.
rationales.7: The rack by the shop door, shelf by shelf is a genuine small-shop idea, and the packet-card art direction carries it into the visuals without borrowed boutique gloss.
rationales.8: The shelf headers and packet illustrations are brand-layer only; nothing near the basket is reinvented.
rationales.9: Two of us keep it stocked, every packet is a variety we grow ourselves is plain and particular enough that a competitor could not lift it unchanged.
rationales.10: Shelves keyed to sowing windows plus the month filter and per-card stock let a repeat visitor see what is sowable and what is available immediately, and both surfaces read as the same shop.
